routes.description: Move from an assumed fundamental reality to God-like perfection by treating unexplained nonmaximal parameters as arbitrary and extending arbitrariness reduction to greatness and other positive attributes.
routes.successCriteria: Establish that foundational limits require explanation, that fundamental reality possesses value or greatness, and that explained or eliminated limits support maximal or quasi-maximal perfection-relevant attributes.

motionBridge.description: Connect the removal of arbitrary foundational limits to maximal or quasi-maximal God-like attributes.

centralBridges.description: Supply reason to expect explanations for apparently arbitrary nonmaximal foundational parameters.
Establish that fundamental reality possesses value, greatness, or a value-entailing capacity.
Show that deeper necessitating grounds do not merely relocate the arbitrariness of limited outcomes.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Specify a comparative or defeasible role for the limits principle when it does not compel a unique worldview.
Restrict arbitrariness inheritance to grounding relations tight enough to transmit the relevant explanatory demand.

routes.description: Block the move from fundamental reality to God-like perfection by treating unexplained limits as one defeasible theoretical consideration and challenging the required explanatory, axiological, and maximality bridges.
routes.successCriteria: Show that rival theories may rationally retain foundational limits, that the foundation need not be minded or valuable, or that explained nonmaximal greatness remains compatible with imperfection.

motionBridge.description: Establish that the limits argument does not by itself determine a God-like or perfect foundation.

centralBridges.description: Require assessment of arbitrary limits within an all-things-considered comparison of rival theories.
Show that the support offered for explaining limits also supports rival principles unless a symmetry breaker is supplied.
Challenge the inference from valuable outcomes or enabling capacities to value or mentality in their foundation.
Preserve the possibility of an explained but nonmaximal degree of foundational greatness.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Clarify the explanatory and modal senses in which a foundational parameter counts as arbitrary.
Test whether arbitrariness inheritance generalizes beyond necessitating grounding without unacceptable consequences.

sections.title: Scope and meaning of arbitrary limits
sections.rationale: This issue fixes what counts as an arbitrary foundational parameter and whether identifying such a parameter establishes a conclusion or instead contributes one consideration to comparative theory choice.

sections.title: Explanatory support and rival-principle parity
sections.rationale: The transition away from limited foundations depends on evidential support for explaining limits and on whether that support survives exceptions and structurally parallel causal principles.

sections.title: Foundation mentality and initial greatness
sections.rationale: Movement toward God-like perfection requires the foundation to possess some value or greatness, making mentality, productive ability, and axiological neutrality burden-relevant alternatives.

sections.title: Grounding value in fundamental reality
sections.rationale: The argument needs a bridge from derivative valuable states to value in their ultimate ground, while the opposing line distinguishes valuable properties from merely necessary enabling conditions.

sections.title: Explained limits and inherited arbitrariness
sections.rationale: The final transition to perfection turns on whether an essential or grounded nonmaximal limit can be nonarbitrary and whether necessitating grounds inherit the arbitrariness they purport to explain.
